questions.q: Which of the three Client Script types is the only one whose return value actually matters?
options: onSubmit, where returning false blocks the save
onLoad, where returning false blocks the page from rendering
onChange, where returning false blocks the field from changing
None of them use a return value
questions.explain: onLoad and onChange don't use a return value to control anything - only onSubmit's return value decides whether the save proceeds.

options: An error message is shown and the record is not saved
The record saves anyway, but with a warning icon
The script throws an exception and crashes the form
justification is automatically filled in with a default value
questions.explain: return false inside onSubmit blocks the save entirely - the record stays open and unsaved.

options: Because onChange also fires once while the form is first loading, which usually isn't the intended trigger
Because isLoading being true means the user's browser has crashed
Because onChange cannot access g_form until isLoading is false
isLoading has no real effect and is only there for documentation
questions.explain: Without the isLoading check, onChange logic would also run during the initial page load, since the field technically 'changes' from nothing to its stored value.

questions.q: If a form has two separate onSubmit scripts, and only one of them returns false, does the record save?
options: No - every onSubmit script runs, and a single false from any of them blocks the save
Yes, because the second script's true return overrides the first
Only the first onSubmit script defined on the form ever actually runs
The platform picks a random one of the two results
questions.explain: ServiceNow runs every onSubmit script on the form; a single false from any of them is enough to block the save.

questions.q: What real parameters does an onChange Client Script receive, beyond the field's control?
options: oldValue, newValue, isLoading, and isTemplate
Only the new value, with no other context
A full GlideRecord of the current record
The HTTP request and response objects
questions.explain: onChange receives control, oldValue, newValue, isLoading, and isTemplate - real context about the change, not just the new value.
